title: A Love Stronger Than Heaven or Hell
note: Adapted directly from author-supplied Parts 1–3; narration lightly condensed for VN pacing. Prologue dialogue is kept in love_beyond_prototype_001.json.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus sat in the damp cave, his body still weak from his life-or-death battle with the angel before him. They had fought so evenly that he now felt no stronger than a mortal man.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: You aren't too bad, angel.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: A cough brought up fresh flecks of blood, a reminder of the angel's might.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The angel regarded him with azure eyes and white pupils that seemed to mimic the endless sky.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: She weakly raised a hand, thumb and pinky extended. Asmodeus watched the familiar gesture for several moments before recognizing it: sign language. The little angel was mute.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: I'm glad you feel the same. We have kinship in that, at least.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel gave him an inquisitive look.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: I'm the demon of lust. I've had perverse encounters with hundreds, perhaps thousands... maybe more people. A few mutes have come my way.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The angel crinkled her nose and waved a hand. He didn't recognize the sign, but its meaning was clear.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Well, regardless, guess we have two options.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: We can work on surviving together until we can get back home, or we can try to kill each other again.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: He would kill her if he had to, but he'd much rather return to his manor. Outings like this weren't his forte.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: I'm Asmodeus, by the way.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The angel considered this for several moments, then traced letters in the air in Enochian.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Now he understood. She wasn't merely an angel, but an archangel—God's grace herself.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Bet the Heaven Father told you to kill some lowly demon.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: She nodded.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: I was told the same. I was told to take out some weak little angel, so I guess we were both punked by our old men.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus sighed and leaned back against the rocky wall. He heard Haniel do the same.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Beneath an old oak, Haniel gathered fallen branches. She lacked her older brother's affinity for flames, and making fire by human means was proving difficult.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The tree was magnificent. Chopping it down would be efficient—but destroying such a life for firewood was unthinkable.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel placed her collection on a patch of bare dirt, where it would damage the forest as little as possible.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus had wandered off early without a word. She couldn't blame him if he'd left; they were natural enemies.

events.speaker: HANIEL [THOUGHT]
events.text: I hope he finds happiness.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Her mission had failed. She doubted Heaven would welcome her back without question.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Yet Asmodeus hadn't killed her in her sleep—or even tried to seduce her. For a demon, his choices were unusual.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: She knelt and rubbed two sticks together. The only thing growing warm was her wrists.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: She sighed. If she had to spend eternity somewhere, at least Earth had grass, birds, and trees unlike her own home.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: A presence approached. Asmodeus emerged, dragging a boar—the fear it had felt before dying still seemed to cling to it.

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: Why would you harm it?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus paused to interpret her hands.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: For us to eat. So we can survive. So we can get stronger.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: He dropped the boar beside the woodpile.

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: It also needed to live. To feel the sun, to eat, to breed.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: But why should we be bound to something so much our lesser? I didn't erase the entire species, just one of many so we can survive as well.

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: Who is to say we are above them?

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: We are stronger. It's the natural order that the strong devour the weak. It happens all the time down here.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: A small flame hovered above Asmodeus's index finger.

events.speaker: HANIEL [SIGNING]
events.text: Then we should know better. Know better and be responsible for ourselves.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: He used the flame to light the pile of wood.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: We should know better?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: She nodded, wondering if she'd gotten through to him.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: To know better than the natural order is a lofty claim, angel. Is that empathy or arrogance?

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel couldn't believe his audacity. His knowing crimson eyes stayed fixed on her.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus butchered the boar with unsettling accuracy and set the meat over the fire. The thought sickened Haniel—but the smell wasn't unappetizing.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus crouched behind a bush, watching a nearby boar. An autumn breeze rustled the leaves and tousled his hair.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Despite Haniel's protests, she had eaten yesterday's meal. Perhaps even angels put survival ahead of principle when they must.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The boar startled and fled, even though Asmodeus had barely moved.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Something heavy and furred slammed into him, hurling him into a tree.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Wind knocked from his lungs, Asmodeus spat flecks of blood and stared at a grizzly bear. In his weakened state, the animal was far stronger.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Shit.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: He stood his ground. Normally his gaze alone would terrify an animal, but the bear showed no fear.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Okay, ugly, let's dance. I would prefer someone cute, but when times are rough you gotta do what you gotta do.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The bear charged. Asmodeus barely dodged its bulk, but a massive paw still struck him and sent him rolling.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Pain racked his body. This time, he couldn't rely on the power of a demon lord.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The bear's overwhelming strength brought Asmodeus down. Every part of him ached, and his body refused to answer.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Alright, ugly, ya got me.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: He had preached survival of the fittest to Haniel only yesterday. Now he seemed destined to learn what that meant from the other side.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The bear loomed above him, one massive paw raised. Asmodeus closed his eyes—not out of fear, but in acceptance.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Wind brushed his face. The bear howled in pain as a brilliant blue arrow struck it.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus opened his eyes. The little angel stood before him, drawing back the string of her invisible bow. Her aim was steady, though she was sweating and weak.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: Haniel...

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: She glanced back at him.

events.speaker: ASMODEUS
events.text: You're shorter than I originally thought.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Haniel rolled her eyes.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The bear charged again. Haniel released her invisible bowstring, and a blue arrow of angelic power struck the beast's head.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: The bear and Haniel hit the ground at the same time.

events.speaker: NARRATOR
events.text: Asmodeus rushed to her and knelt by her side. The angel who had argued for the life of a boar yesterday had killed a creature today—for him. A demon.

ending.note: No Part Four script has been supplied yet.
